steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Design brief: a concise statement of the problem to be solved - identifies the user, the need and the context. Not a solution - a starting point. | Key Fact: Design specification: a list of measurable criteria the product must meet - function, target user, dimensions, materials, cost, safety, aesthetics, environmental impact. Must be testable. | Key Fact: User research: interviews, questionnaires, observation, focus groups - reveals real needs, not assumptions. Ask open questions, observe users in context, identify pain points. | Key Fact: Market research: analyse competing products - features, price points, materials, strengths, weaknesses. Identify gaps in the market and opportunities for innovation.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Write a design brief and three specification points for a product that helps elderly people open jar lids. | Explain the difference between a design brief and a design specification. | A designer wants to create a new type of school bag. Describe three research methods they should use and explain what each would reveal.
